title: Sunita Shukla v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Surya Prakash Kesarwani, J.; Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; relegated to fresh Clause 6.8 objection.
headnote: A consumer challenged an electricity demand and recovery notice as issued without considering her objection. Without opining on merits, the High Court disposed of the writ with liberty to file a fresh objection under Clause 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, to be decided by a reasoned speaking order within four weeks after opportunity of hearing.
facts: Sunita Shukla petitioned the Allahabad High Court alleging that respondent no. 2 had raised an electricity demand and issued a recovery notice without considering her objection. Counsel for the respondents submitted that she could move a fresh objection under Clause 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which would be considered within a time-bound period after a reasonable opportunity of hearing. The Division Bench heard counsel for the petitioner and the Standing Counsel for the State.

holding_units.holding: Without expressing any opinion on merits, the writ was disposed of with liberty to file a fresh objection under Clause 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within three weeks; if so filed, the licensee shall decide it by a reasoned speaking order within four weeks after reasonable opportunity of hearing.

principle_tags.application: The Court did not decide the demand or recovery notice and instead relegated the consumer to a fresh Clause 6.8 objection, with a time-bound speaking order after hearing.

not_decided.point: Validity of the electricity demand and recovery notice, and whether the earlier objection had been considered
not_decided.note: Court expressly declined to opine on merits.
